title: Third Wheel in Space — Mr. & Mrs. X #2

events.speaker: NARRATOR
events.text: A small ship is tumbling out of orbit, trailing smoke, falling toward a rust-red planet nobody back home has ever heard of. Somewhere above it, a man in handcuffs is watching it go down.

events.speaker: NARRATOR
events.text: That man is Remy LeBeau, Gambit. And the woman on that falling ship is his wife of about a week.

events.speaker: GAMBIT
events.text: Rogue, I'm countin' on dat invulnerability.
spaceship crash impact, huge, debris

events.speaker: NARRATOR
events.text: The ship hits the dirt hard. And when the dust settles, the first figure to climb out of the wreckage isn't Rogue. It's a man in a red suit, coughing.

events.speaker: DEADPOOL
events.text: Space is so dumb.

events.speaker: NARRATOR
events.text: So, yes. Deadpool is on Rogue's honeymoon. Let's talk about how we got here.

events.speaker: NARRATOR
events.text: Welcome back. Today we're covering Mister and Missus X, issue two, part two of the "Love and Marriage" arc. It's written by Kelly Thompson, with art by Oscar Bazaldua, colors by Frank D'Armata, and a cover by Terry and Rachel Dodson that tells you exactly what kind of issue this is going to be.

events.speaker: NARRATOR
events.text: Quick catch-up. Rogue and Gambit have been on and off for longer than some of you have been alive. When their friends Kitty and Piotr called off their own wedding at the altar, Remy and Rogue looked at each other and decided not to waste the chapel. Surprise wedding. Done.

events.speaker: NARRATOR
events.text: For the honeymoon, they went to space, because of course they did. And then Kitty asked them for a small favor: pick up a mysterious package. That package turned out to be something the Shi'ar Imperial Guard very badly wanted back. In the scramble, Rogue blacked out, and woke up next to Deadpool.

events.speaker: NARRATOR
events.text: So we open on the bridge of the couple's honeymoon ship, which the Imperial Guard has, let's say, borrowed. Gambit is their prisoner. Gladiator, the Guard's leader, has a lock on the package, and on a cloaked vessel right next to it.

events.speaker: NARRATOR
events.text: Gambit warns them that if they open fire, they could destroy the very thing they're after. Gladiator's answer is cold and simple: better it's destroyed than in the wrong hands. He gives the order to shoot.
laser cannon blast, sci-fi

events.speaker: NARRATOR
events.text: And they hit it. The cloaked ship breaks apart and drops toward the planet below, and Remy, who knows exactly who's on board, can only watch.

events.speaker: NARRATOR
events.text: But Gambit had quietly picked his cuffs, and he wasn't the only prisoner with a trick. Deathbird, the Shi'ar exile riding along in custody, had a bio-signature teleporter the guards missed when they searched her. She tells Gambit she can remove the whole Imperial Guard from the equation, but she'll have to go with them. And Remy, who has a wife falling out of the sky, says do whatever it takes.
teleport whoosh, sci-fi shimmer

events.speaker: NARRATOR
events.text: One flash later, the bridge is empty except for one very angry Cajun. He grabs the controls and heads straight down.

events.speaker: NARRATOR
events.text: Down on the surface, Rogue walks out of the smoke without a scratch. Deadpool, meanwhile, is missing a spleen, and he wants credit for it. It turns out it was Deadpool's teleport beam that pulled Rogue out of open space. So he did save her life, and he will not stop mentioning it.

events.speaker: NARRATOR
events.text: Rogue asks the obvious question: what are you doing here, Wade? And his answer is that the package is his. Except it's not a package to him. It's an egg.

events.speaker: DEADPOOL
events.text: No, I'm here to get my egg.

events.speaker: NARRATOR
events.text: Here's what makes this scene work. These two have history. Back in their Avengers days, Rogue and Deadpool shared a kiss, and Thompson knows we remember it. So every line Wade says is a little flirt, a little guilt trip. He's hurt he wasn't invited to the wedding. He thinks a hundred-million-dollar egg sounds like a reasonable wedding gift for himself.

events.speaker: NARRATOR
events.text: Rogue doesn't take the bait. Then Gambit lands, relieved and confused in equal measure, and hears the name "Deadpool." He doesn't get to react before Rogue looks down at her empty bag.

events.speaker: ROGUE
events.text: Oh, sonofa— He got the egg.

events.speaker: NARRATOR
events.text: Wade is already sprinting for their ship, egg tucked under his arm like a football. And Remy turns to his bride with a very polite question.

events.speaker: GAMBIT
events.text: Do I have your permission ta blow him up, chère?

events.speaker: NARRATOR
events.text: Rogue says yes, just keep it light until she has the egg. Remy does not keep it light. He admits he's adding a little extra for that kiss, and for crashing the honeymoon.
explosion, energy blast, magical

events.speaker: NARRATOR
events.text: Rogue snatches the egg out of the air, and we get our first real look. That glowing crystal they were guarding was just the case. A Shi'ar briefcase. Inside is an actual egg. Remy's verdict: Kitty is trolling them. Who makes newlyweds babysit an egg on their honeymoon?

events.speaker: NARRATOR
events.text: Deadpool, of course, regenerates in a minute flat and comes back threatening to slice them into little cubes. Rogue calls his bluff. He doesn't need the egg, she says. He wants the money, and those are not the same thing. Then she punches him across the desert.

events.speaker: NARRATOR
events.text: Wade's comeback is that, on his way down, he left a grenade on her belt.
grenade explosion, close

events.speaker: NARRATOR
events.text: Rogue is fine. Rogue is always fine. But this is the moment Gambit runs out of patience with Wade Wilson, and honestly, so do we.

events.speaker: NARRATOR
events.text: And while the three of them are wrestling in the dirt over a fragile egg, someone else shows up. Technet. If you've never met them, think of the strangest bounty hunters in the galaxy, all in one team photo.

events.speaker: NARRATOR
events.text: There's China Doll, who shrinks anything she touches. Gatecrasher, a huge telepath and the boss, whose little teleporter sidekick Yap calls her Mother. Waxworks, who melts bodies into wax. Bodybag, who coats you in paralyzing slime. And Joyboy, a creepy baby in an eggshell who turns your desires into nightmares. Also, they want the egg.

events.speaker: NARRATOR
events.text: So the bickering stops, and the three of them call a truce. Deadpool gives Gambit a new nickname while they're at it. Let's just say it's a brand of aftershave, and Remy does not love it.

events.speaker: NARRATOR
events.text: Rogue takes command right away. Hit the big one first, she says, because Gatecrasher and Yap can shut you down from a distance. And of course she gets blindsided mid-sentence, which Deadpool finds hilarious.

events.speaker: NARRATOR
events.text: Gambit, meanwhile, goes straight for Gatecrasher. A face full of charged cards, a polite apology, and a reminder that his bride said she has to go.

events.speaker: NARRATOR
events.text: Joyboy tries to get into Deadpool's head and finds out the hard way that Wade's head is the last place you want to be. The baby screams and bails. Then China Doll shrinks Gambit down to action-figure size, and Rogue lands on her with one fist.

events.speaker: ROGUE
events.text: China Doll, I like my man the size he is.

events.speaker: NARRATOR
events.text: Next, Waxworks gets his hands on Rogue and reshapes her into something out of a nightmare, and Deadpool can't stop commenting until Gambit asks if he's ever been quiet in his life. The answer is no. Rogue pulls herself back together, literally, and announces she's done.

events.speaker: NARRATOR
events.text: And this is the best Rogue moment in the issue. She grabs Yap, absorbs his teleportation power, and instead of beating Technet to a pulp, she sends the whole team somewhere safe with a warning not to come back. Gatecrasher's parting shot is ominous, though. Word is out about this egg, and everything in the Shi'ar galaxy is coming for it.
teleport zap, electric

events.speaker: NARRATOR
events.text: Back on the ship, Deadpool has his feet up like he paid for the trip. He wants a ride to the nearest outpost, with his egg. Gambit lays out the bill: you crashed our honeymoon, you blew up my bride, and we're not even going to talk about the kissing.

events.speaker: NARRATOR
events.text: Rogue is gentler, but just as firm. She thanks Wade for saving her life, and tells him the egg goes back to the X-Men. No arguments. She's asking him to walk away. Wade asks what he gets for that, and she gives him a look.

events.speaker: ROGUE
events.text: Wade. Don't test me.

events.speaker: DEADPOOL
events.text: But that's my favorite.

events.speaker: GAMBIT
events.text: This is the honeymoon of my nightmares.

events.speaker: NARRATOR
events.text: And then Wade mentions, very casually, that the egg is cracked. And that he didn't do it.
eggshell cracking, glassy

events.speaker: NARRATOR
events.text: Light pours out of the shell. Wade was hoping for a dragon. What steps out is a young woman, barefoot and glowing, with the same white streak in her hair as Rogue, looking right at her. And she asks them, very softly, to help her.

events.speaker: DEADPOOL
events.text: That is so much better than a dragon!

events.speaker: NARRATOR
events.text: Here's my take on this issue. On paper it's a chase comic. A package, a bounty, a fight in the desert. But Kelly Thompson is really writing about the first week of a marriage. Gambit's jealousy is right there on the surface. Rogue's past keeps walking into the room, and she keeps choosing to handle it instead of hiding it. And the big joke is that the more Deadpool tries to come between them, the more they work like a team.

events.speaker: NARRATOR
events.text: Then Thompson drops a girl who looks like Rogue out of an egg, and suddenly the honeymoon has a whole new question hanging over it. Who is she? Where did she come from? And why does the entire Shi'ar galaxy want her?

events.speaker: NARRATOR
events.text: I've got theories, but I want yours first. Tell me in the comments who you think she is. If you enjoyed this, hit like and subscribe, because next time, the honeymoon gets even stranger. See you there.
